In October 2023, Apple issued threat notifications to iPhone users who may have been targeted by spyware attacks. More than 20 journalists and opposition politicians in India were reported to have received the notifications. Forensic investigations of the devices later revealed that Pegasus spyware had been used to target these devices.

(6/7)

The @DoT_India notified the Telecommunications (User Identification) Rules, 2026 (“the Rules”) on 21 August 2026. The Rules mandate that telecom operators verify the facial biometric information of every person who chooses to obtain a new SIM, replace or change their details, or even surrender their number. 

(1/n)
#privacy #surveillance #biometric

It seems that the Rules, along with the circular, aim to revive the same mandates that have been struck down as illegal and unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in the past.

(9/n)
#privacy #surveillance #biometric

Such measures present a grave threat to the fundamental right to privacy for millions of Indians, as it requires private entities to collect and process troves of biometric information based on justifications that fail to satisfy the test of proportionality and necessity.

(10/n)
#privacy #surveillance #biometric

https://t.co/fQcMLwYL9X, a crowdsourced platform created to anonymously document alleged demands for bribes has been temporarily taken offline, citing concerns around traffic, data security, spam, duplicate entries, and misuse.

The public disclosure of alleged demands has also raised questions about the criminal liability of complainants. Under the Prevention of Corruption Act, bribing a public servant is punishable with up to seven years’ imprisonment. Those who report the demand within seven days are exempt from punishment. However, a public disclosure on a website falls outside that protection.

Speaking to @timesofindia, https://t.co/X7ipfsWjp2 founder @mishichoudhary highlights the importance of data minimisation, security by design, and anonymity on such platforms to protect complainants' identities.

text:
From real time facial recognition vans to a web of CCTV cameras to Meta glasses, state #surveillance paraphernalia was on full display during the #studentprotests! What does this mean for our rights to #privacy & #dissent?  

@internetfreedom, @najarjustice and @no2uid are organising a Webinar to understand state surveillance during students protests, its implications for our rights and how we can resist.

Speakers include @Aditi_muses, @digitaldutta and @apar1984

Friday, 28 August, 6.30pm - 8pm  
Link to register - https://t.co/JFOq0S9X94  

Join this important discussion.

A new DoT regime makes live biometric verification mandatory for getting, replacing, updating or even surrendering a SIM. Aadhaar holders must use Aadhaar e-KYC, while a new Digital Intelligence Platform will circulate subscribers’ representative images between telecom operators to enforce a cap on connections. IFF believes this creates a nationwide biometric surveillance infrastructure without adequate legal safeguards. (1/7)  

Read More: https://t.co/NkQnGxwWdW

The government says the objective is to combat cyber fraud. But fraud is driven heavily by social engineering, mule accounts, WhatsApp and spoofed or international numbers. Meanwhile, targeted systems such as ASTR and Chakshu have already been used to disconnect suspected SIMs without subjecting every subscriber to mandatory biometrics. Less intrusive tools already exist. (6/7)

IFF had written to the DoT about these risks when the Rules were still a draft, seeking genuine choice between e-KYC and D-KYC, purpose limitation, retention limits and safeguards against creating another biometric database. The final Rules do not address these concerns. We will pursue RTIs, representations and parliamentary outreach, while assessing legal options. If biometric verification has blocked you from getting, keeping or transferring a SIM, write to legal@internetfreedom.in. (7/7)

Support our work: https://t.co/qSG7IzUpIX

Your phone number is now tied to banking, UPI, Aadhaar OTPs, DigiLocker, ration e-KYC and welfare payments. Under the Telecommunications (User Identification) Rules, 2026, a failed face, fingerprint or iris verification can therefore become more than a failed authentication. It can prevent someone from getting, replacing, updating or transferring a connection. (2/7)
